items.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: I have a wish someday to write for the New York City Ballet, for this choreographer, Christopher Wheeldon, who I love.

ctx.x: Can you think ahead five years?

Not really, not really. I know I don’t like to take commissions too far ahead, because sometimes I think wow, if I wanted to move to Rio in two years I want to be able to do that. For instance, I like having an apartment. Because I like the idea, even though I’ve been there for several years now, I like the idea that if I just wanted to pick up and do something new I could. That my life isn’t so, you know, stuck in some physical thing that I can’t just like move out of it. And the same is musically. I know a few…

changing so drastically or for whatever reason, she doesn’t really know exactly, and she cites five womens’ lives, how women tend to maybe set sort of a fuzzy goal or maybe a strong goal, but often in their lives other things come in that take them to drastically new places. And she talks about life as being an improvisation. And so sometimes — I never expected really to be doing this, what I’m doing. I had no real idea, no set path, it just kind of happened.
